statement: A heuristic function h(n), representing the estimated distance from node n to the goal node, is consistent if, whenever a node is removed from open_set during A* search, the path to it is guaranteed to be optimal, ensuring that the test 'tentative_g_score < g_score[neighbor]' will always fail if the node is reached again.

symbols.meaning: heuristic function, the estimated distance from node n to the goal node
distance from the start node to node n
a node in the search graph
the set of candidate nodes to be expanded in A*
tentative distance/cost score to a neighbor node via a candidate path
recorded lowest distance/cost score from start to neighbor

properties.property: When a node is removed from open_set, the path found to it is guaranteed to be optimal.
properties.why: the test 'tentative_g_score < g_score[neighbor]' will always fail if the node is reached again

properties.property: Nodes removed from open_set never need to be re-added to open_set.
properties.why: optimal paths to closed nodes are already guaranteed upon first removal

properties.property: The tree-search version of A* (which does not re-add nodes to open_set) is guaranteed to find optimal paths.
properties.why: tree-search omits the test to add nodes back to open_set and requires a consistent heuristic for optimality

properties.property: A* is optimally efficient with respect to all admissible A*-like search algorithms on non-pathological problems.
properties.why: no admissible A*-like algorithm can expand fewer nodes than A* when the heuristic is consistent and tie-breaking is suitably chosen

assumptions.assumption: The cost of a path is the sum of its costs, or the problem satisfies the conditions of a cost algebra.
assumptions.breaks_when: The path cost cannot be formed by summation of edge costs or violates the conditions of a cost algebra.

assumptions.assumption: A*'s tie-breaking rule is suitably chosen.
assumptions.breaks_when: An unsuitable tie-breaking rule allows an alternative algorithm to expand fewer nodes.

assumptions.assumption: The search problem is non-pathological (up to tie-breaking).
assumptions.breaks_when: Pathological problem instances occur where optimal efficiency guarantees fail.

failure_modes.mode: Suboptimal path returned by tree-search A*
failure_modes.signature: Tree-search A* terminates with a path that is not least-cost.
failure_modes.cause: The heuristic function is admissible but not consistent, and nodes reached via subsequent cheaper paths cannot be re-added to open_set.

failure_modes.mode: Arbitrary node expansion overhead (loss of optimal efficiency)
failure_modes.signature: A* expands arbitrarily more nodes than an alternative admissible A*-like search algorithm.
failure_modes.cause: The heuristic function is admissible but not consistent on a non-pathological search problem.
